ordered_diagnoses: Metastatic disease to thyroid from other primary site

s1.syndrome_frame: Neck mass with dysphagia and pain, with a history of previous malignancy
salient_findings: Large, firm, mildly tender mass on the right side of the neck
Positive Pemberton sign
Hypo- to anechoic mass replacing the right thyroid lobe on ultrasound
Fine-needle aspiration biopsy suspicious for primary or secondary malignancy
Pulmonary nodules consistent with metastases on CT
key_facts: History of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans excision in 1998
Right lobe volume of 50 mL on ultrasound
Left lobe volume of 7.3 mL on ultrasound
Hemorrhagic background with isolated clusters of pleomorphic round and oval nuclei on fine-needle aspiration biopsy
Category IV/3, suspicious for primary or secondary malignancy on biopsy
Voluminous right thyroid mass on CT
Two pulmonary nodules consistent with metastases on CT
Freely mobile vocal cords on laryngoscopy

raw.rationale: The patient's history of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans excision and multiple local recurrences, combined with the presence of a large, firm mass in the thyroid and pulmonary nodules consistent with metastases, suggests that the thyroid mass is a metastasis from the patient's known primary malignancy.

rejected.label: Papillary thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: While possible, the patient's history and the presence of metastatic disease suggest a secondary malignancy is more likely.

rejected.label: Follicular thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: Similar to papillary thyroid carcinoma, follicular thyroid carcinoma is a primary thyroid malignancy, but the patient's history suggests a metastasis is more likely.

rejected.label: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma is an aggressive primary thyroid malignancy, but the patient's history and the presence of metastatic disease suggest a secondary malignancy is more likely.

rejected.label: Metastatic disease to thyroid from other primary site
rejected.why: While the patient does have metastatic disease, the history of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans suggests that this is the primary site, making 'Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans metastasis to thyroid' a more specific and likely diagnosis.
